title: adaptive-dequeue-backoff-continuous-batcher
author: Aisha Verma
description:
Motivation: Continuous-batcher workloads have exhibited intermittent KV-pin starvation where long-lived KV-heavy requests repeatedly preempt short requests due to deterministic dequeue ordering. This causes tail latency spikes for small requests and degrades 95th/99th percentile SLOs. This PR introduces an adaptive dequeue backoff algorithm and a lightweight starvation score metric to smooth fairness without sacrificing throughput.

What this PR does: Adds an adaptive 'dequeue backoff' policy that injects a variable delay/jitter when a queue has consumed consecutive slots beyond an expectation threshold. The backoff duration is proportional to a starvation_score computed from queue hold-time, recent slot usage, and KV-pin weight. The policy is kernel-aware (hints to the runtime when large kv- pinned workloads are present) so the scheduler can prefer low-KV lanes under tight latency SLOs.

Design summary: - starvation_score: rolling counter decayed over 10s window combining (consecutive_slots, avg_exec_ms, kv_pin_weight) - backoff calculation: min_backoff + log(1 + starvation_score) * scale, jittered to avoid synchronization - kernel hints: continuous_batcher exposes light/heavy hints; the kernel scheduler can favor different execution kernels or quantized paths for heavy requests - config: new config block continuousBatcher.adaptiveBackoff with tunables and a safety cap to avoid starving throughput-critical lanes.

Testing & validation: Unit tests for backoff math and starvation score decay. Integration test that replays real production traces (small/large mix) showing reduced 99th latency for short requests. Benchmarks on p4d: baseline vs this change with mixed workload (75% small, 25% kv-heavy): 99th latency for small requests reduced from 312ms -> 188ms (40% improvement) with <2% throughput regression.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag gated, gradual canary by region: 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Observability added: continuous.batcher.backoff_ms, continuous.batcher.starvation_score, continuous.batcher.backoff_count. Alert added to SLO dashboard to detect regressions (increase in mean backoff_ms > 20% on canary).

Related: Implements ENG-4822 (scheduling fairness workstream). References in-code tickets and design doc at docs/design/continuous-batcher-backoff.md.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the default backoff conservative to avoid oscillation; future work includes auto-tuning scale per-tenant and integrating with autoscaler signals.
